To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total affected depth of microhardened sub-surface layer of machined surface is a function of the main WEDM parameters: discharge current, pulse-on time, and wire feed rate.
the total microhardened layer thickness and its homogeneity can be significantly influenced by the main WEDM parameters, such as discharge voltage, discharge current, and pulse on-time.
the microhardened surface layers of machined surfaces can be reduced by the proper selection of the main WEDM process parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of the main WEDM parameters, namely, the wire feed, the pulse-on time, the pulse-off time, the discharge voltage, the wire tension and the wire speed, on the microhardening of the machined material surface.
the influence of WEDM technological process parameters on microhardened surface layers and the final quality of machinable surfaces.
the influence of the main technological parameters on the total depth and on the variation depth of microhardened layer of machined surface of tool steel EN 1.2081.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WEDM is a process that is able to generate microhardened surface layers on machined surfaces.

WEDM is a very effective machining method for tool steel materials, but the resulting quality of the machined surfaces is very strongly influenced by the microhardened surface layers that occur after WEDM process.
the WEDM process with brass wire electrode has the potential to be a very effective method for surface microhardening, especially when a high quality of the surface finish is not required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microhardness values of machined surface of tool steel EN 1.2082 (X210Cr12) were significantly influenced by the main technological parameters (voltage, current, wire feed rate, pulse-on time, and pulse-off time) of the discharge process.
the WEDM process can be considered as a very effective and precise method to produce thin microhardened layers on tool steel EN X 210Cr12 (1.2080).
the WEDM process is suitable for machining of tool steels, and that it is possible to obtain a machined surface with a thin, homogeneous microhardened surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microhardened surface layers are not a problem in the machining process, but they have an influence on the quality of the machined surfaces.

the microhardened surface layers of the machined material surface can be minimized by setting the main WEDM process parameters in a way to achieve the lowest total microhardened layer depth and the lowest microhardened layer homogeneity.

WEDM process is an effective method for machining of hard materials, but the microhardened surface layers that are formed on machined surface have to be taken into account when the surface integrity of a machined workpiece is evaluated.
